questions.question: Which characteristic best defines a Class 2 circuit as distinct from a Class 1 circuit?
options: A) It always operates at exactly 24 V
B) It is supplied from a power-limited source so both voltage and power are inherently limited
C) It requires conductors no smaller than #14 AWG
D) It must always be run in a raceway
questions.answer: It is supplied from a power-limited source so both voltage and power are inherently limited. Class 2 circuits are defined by the limited energy of their power source, which is what makes them safe with very small conductors.
solution_steps: Class 2 vs Class 1 — Rule 16-200 hinges on the power source.
Fast path: Class 2 = power-limited source (voltage and power capped).

questions.question: A Class 2 power source operates at 50 V. What is the maximum overcurrent (fuse) value permitted on its output?
questions.answer: 2.0 A. A Class 2 source above 30 V is limited to 100 VA, so at 50 V the maximum current = 100 VA / 50 V = 2.0 A.
solution_steps: Power limit — Rule 16-200: Class 2 above 30 V is capped at 100 VA.
Fast path: 100 VA / 50 V = 2.0 A.

questions.question: What is the smallest conductor size permitted for a Class 1 remote-control or signal circuit?
questions.answer: #18 AWG. Class 1 circuits are not power-limited like Class 2, so the smallest permitted conductor is #18 AWG (with #16 also common), well above the #30 AWG allowed for Class 2.
solution_steps: Class 1 conductor sizing — Rule 16-210.
Fast path: smallest Class 1 = #18 AWG (Class 2 goes down to #30).

questions.question: What is the maximum overcurrent protection permitted for a #16 AWG conductor in a Class 1 circuit that extends beyond the equipment enclosure?
questions.answer: 7 A. Rule 16-210 limits a #16 AWG Class 1 conductor extending beyond the enclosure to 7 A overcurrent protection (a #18 AWG conductor is limited to 5 A).
solution_steps: Small Class 1 conductor overcurrent — Rule 16-210.
Fast path: #16 max 7 A, #18 max 5 A.

questions.question: A Class 1 extra-low-voltage power circuit is limited to which maximum power?
questions.answer: 1000 VA. Rule 16-200 limits a Class 1 extra-low-voltage power circuit (max 30 V) to a maximum source power of 1000 VA.
solution_steps: Class 1 ELV power source — Rule 16-200.
Fast path: 30 V and 1000 VA for Class 1 ELV power.

questions.question: Where neither circuit is in a raceway, what minimum separation is required between Class 2 conductors and a 600 V power circuit?
questions.answer: 600 mm. For power circuits above the basic threshold (such as 600 V) where neither circuit is in a raceway, Rule 16-212 requires a 600 mm separation from Class 2 conductors.
solution_steps: Separation by voltage — Rule 16-212.
Fast path: higher voltage power = 600 mm; ≤300 V = 50 mm.

questions.question: The 50 mm / 600 mm separation requirements between Class 2 and power conductors in Rule 16-212 apply specifically under what condition?
options: A) Only when both circuits are inside the same raceway
B) Where neither circuit is installed in a raceway
C) Only for circuits above 750 V
questions.answer: Where neither circuit is installed in a raceway. The open-wiring separation distances apply when the conductors are not enclosed in a raceway that would otherwise provide separation.
solution_steps: When does separation distance apply — Rule 16-212.
Fast path: applies where neither circuit is in a raceway.

questions.question: What maximum voltage defines an extra-low-voltage (ELV) circuit in Section 16?
questions.answer: 30 V. Extra-low-voltage means a voltage not exceeding 30 V, which is the key boundary for Class 1 and Class 2 ELV circuits in Section 16.
solution_steps: ELV boundary — Rule 16-200.
Fast path: ELV = not over 30 V.

questions.question: Class 2 wiring methods (such as Type ELC conductors and the reduced separation rules) may be applied only where the circuit meets what requirement?
options: A) The circuit voltage is at least 120 V
B) The circuit is supplied from a Class 2 power-limited source
C) The conductors are #14 AWG or larger
D) The circuit is a fire alarm circuit
questions.answer: The circuit is supplied from a Class 2 power-limited source. Only circuits fed from an approved Class 2 power-limited source may use Class 2 wiring methods; otherwise Class 1 (or power) wiring rules apply.
solution_steps: Where Class 2 methods apply — Rule 16-200/16-210.
Fast path: requires a Class 2 power-limited source.

questions.question: A 24 V fire alarm initiating-device circuit must be wired as which class of circuit?
options: A) Class 2, because it operates at 24 V (extra-low-voltage)
B) Class 2, because the panel limits the power
C) Class 1, because fire alarm is a life-safety circuit
D) Unclassified, because it is a signalling circuit
questions.answer: Class 1, because fire alarm is a life-safety circuit. Fire alarm circuits are treated as Class 1 regardless of their low 24 V operating voltage.
solution_steps: Fire alarm classification — Rule 16-100 / Section 32.
Fast path: fire alarm = Class 1 even at 24 V.

questions.question: Type TEW conductors are intended for use in which application?
options: A) Open Class 2 field wiring without a raceway
B) Within equipment enclosures or in raceways (equipment/appliance wire)
C) Direct burial as a Class 2 cable
D) As an approved fire alarm cable
questions.answer: Within equipment enclosures or in raceways. Type TEW is equipment/appliance wire and is not an approved open Class 2 cable; field wiring without a raceway must use a cable approved for the purpose such as Type ELC.
solution_steps: Conductor type TEW — Rule 16-210.
Fast path: TEW = equipment wire, use in enclosures/raceways, not open Class 2.

questions.question: When determining the ampacity of an ELC or LVT cable, what is the effect of increasing the number of conductors in the cable?
options: D) The conductors must be upsized to #14 AWG
questions.answer: The ampacity is derated (reduced). Table 11 gives the base #16 AWG ampacity, which is reduced as the number of conductors in the cable increases because of the added heat.
solution_steps: ELC/LVT ampacity vs conductor count — Table 11.
Fast path: more conductors = more heat = lower ampacity (derated).

questions.question: What is the smallest conductor size permitted in a Class 2 power-limited circuit?
questions.answer: #30 AWG. Because Class 2 circuits are power-limited, Rule 16-210 permits conductors as small as #30 AWG.
solution_steps: Class 2 minimum conductor — Rule 16-210.
Fast path: power-limited allows down to #30 AWG.

questions.question: Where neither circuit is in a raceway, what minimum separation is required between Class 2 conductors and a 120 V lighting branch circuit?
questions.answer: 50 mm. A 120 V circuit is at or below the 300 V threshold, so Rule 16-212 requires the basic 50 mm separation where neither circuit is in a raceway.
solution_steps: Separation at low voltage — Rule 16-212.
Fast path: ≤300 V = 50 mm separation.

questions.question: Unlike a Class 2 circuit, a Class 1 circuit (other than an extra-low-voltage power circuit) is characterized by which of the following?
options: A) Its power source is not inherently power-limited, so overcurrent protection and conductor sizing govern
B) It is always limited to 100 VA
C) It may never exceed 30 V
D) It must use #30 AWG conductors
questions.answer: Its power source is not inherently power-limited, so overcurrent protection and conductor sizing govern. Class 1 circuits rely on standard conductor sizing and overcurrent protection rather than a power-limited source like Class 2.
solution_steps: Class 1 vs Class 2 energy — Rule 16-200.
Fast path: Class 1 is not power-limited; conductor size and overcurrent protection apply.
